chief_complaint: severe chronic suprapubic pain relieved directly by urination with extreme urinary frequency
hpi_details: 38F presenting with 2-year history of debilitating bladder pain worsening as bladder fills and relieved immediately upon voiding up to 25 times daily, with negative urine cultures and glomerulations/Hunner lesions seen on hydrodistension cystoscopy.
ideas: She thinks the inner lining of her bladder has become raw and ulcerated like severe heartburn inside her pelvis.
concerns: She is terrified that this relentless agony will destroy her marriage and force her to quit her job because she cannot sit still for twenty minutes.
expectations: She hopes to receive a targeted bladder instillation or medication that coats the bladder wall so she can get through a work shift.

available_results.value: Nitrite negative; leukocyte esterase negative; blood negative

clinical_knowledge.topic: Interstitial Cystitis Bladder Pain Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a clinical diagnosis of bladder-related pain with lower urinary tract symptoms for more than 6 weeks, after infection and other causes are excluded.
Document baseline voiding frequency, pain, hematuria, pelvic symptoms, and validated symptom scores; urinalysis and culture are needed when infection is possible.
Cystoscopy is not required for an uncomplicated presentation, but Hunner lesions support the diagnosis and change treatment; glomerulations alone are nonspecific.

Use shared, stepwise multimodal management: education, avoidance of individual triggers, bladder training when tolerated, stress management, and pelvic-floor physical therapy for tenderness; avoid strengthening/Kegel exercises when the pelvic floor is hypertonic.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe chronic suprapubic pain relieved directly by urination with extreme urinary frequency

Key HPI features: 38F presenting with 2-year history of debilitating bladder pain worsening as bladder fills and relieved immediately upon voiding up to 25 times daily, with negative urine cultures and glomerulations/Hunner lesions seen on hydrodistension cystoscopy.

Objective/Exam findings: Obtain vital signs; abdominal and pelvic examination (including pelvic-floor tenderness), urinalysis and urine culture. Consider pregnancy testing, STI evaluation, cytology or hematuria evaluation only when indicated by history/risk.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Interstitial Cystitis Bladder Pain Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Urinary tract infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Attributing new fever, flank pain, vomiting, or systemic illness to IC/BPS instead of urgently evaluating for pyelonephritis or an obstructed infected system.
Dismissing gross hematuria, persistent microscopic hematuria, weight loss, or a pelvic mass; these require evaluation for malignancy, stones, or other pathology.
Treating repeated negative cultures with antibiotics or starting bladder-directed therapy before excluding infection and pregnancy when relevant.
Prescribing amitriptyline, hydroxyzine, or other sedating/anticholinergic medicines without reviewing sedation, falls, urinary retention, QT risk, and drug interactions.
management_principles: Confirm no infection or alternative urgent diagnosis, then establish a baseline symptom/voiding diary and individualized goals.
Start conservative measures and refer for pelvic-floor physical therapy when tender or hypertonic; offer urology/urogynecology follow-up for persistent or complex symptoms.
Discuss medications and procedures as individualized options rather than routine first-line treatment; reassess benefit and adverse effects regularly.
Treat documented Hunner lesions with urologist-directed endoscopic therapy; rapidly escalate fever, flank pain, anuria/retention, severe uncontrolled pain, or systemic illness.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Interstitial Cystitis Bladder Pain Syndrome: severe chronic suprapubic pain relieved directly by urination with extreme urinary frequency. 38F presenting with 2-year history of debilitating bladder pain worsening as bladder fills and relieved immediately upon voiding up to 25 times daily, with negative urine cultures and glomerulations/Hunner lesions seen on hydrodistension cystoscopy.
reference_soap.objective: Obtain vital signs; abdominal and pelvic examination including pelvic-floor assessment; urinalysis and urine culture. Evaluate hematuria, pregnancy, STI risk, or atypical features when indicated.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Interstitial Cystitis Bladder Pain Syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: Exclude infection and other causes; record a voiding/pain diary. Begin education, individualized trigger avoidance, stress management, and pelvic-floor physical therapy when indicated; arrange urology follow-up for Hunner-lesion-directed treatment and persistent symptoms. Seek urgent evaluation for fever, flank pain, vomiting, inability to void, gross hematuria, or systemic illness.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features and diagnostic criteria of Interstitial Cystitis Bladder Pain Syndrome
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for severe chronic suprapubic pain relieved directly by urination with extreme urinary frequency
Select appropriate laboratory and imaging studies for urology
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies

teaching.one_liner: Urology evaluation for patient presenting with severe chronic suprapubic pain relieved directly by urination with extreme urinary frequency.
differentials: Endometriosis or chronic pelvic pain syndrome

must_ask.objective: Pain relationship to bladder filling and voiding
must_ask.say: Does the pain get worse as your bladder fills up, and does it go away right after you urinate?
How many times a day do you need to urinate, and how is that affecting your daily life?

must_ask.objective: Exclude infection - dysuria, fever, prior culture results
must_ask.say: Have your urine tests come back negative for infection, and do you have any fever or burning?
Have you noticed certain foods or drinks, like coffee, alcohol, or spicy food, that make the pain worse?
How long have you been dealing with this pain and frequency — is it more than six months?

history.answer: Doctor, my lower belly aches terribly as my bladder fills, and I have to run to the bathroom more than twenty times a day just to get relief.
It does not sting or burn sharply when the urine flows; it is a deep, aching pressure in my lower pelvis that builds up before I go.
This started about two years ago and has gradually become so severe that it dominates my whole life.
Doctors kept giving me antibiotics for suspected bladder infections, but the urine tests were always negative and the pills never helped.
The pain builds up steadily as my bladder fills with urine, and emptying my bladder relieves the pain right away.
My urine is usually clear and straw-colored, and I have never seen any blood or cloudy sediment in it.
No, my urine smells completely normal without any foul or pungent odor.
I have to urinate up to twenty-five times a day and get up four or five times each night because the urgent pressure is unbearable.
I can start my stream without hesitation and the flow is normal, but my bladder starts aching again just minutes after finishing.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or sweating episodes.
No, I have never had any flank pain or aching in my back.
Yes, there is intense aching and pressure right over my pubic bone that gets worse as urine collects.
No, I have not felt nauseated and I have not vomited.
No, I do not have any unusual vaginal discharge, odor, or itching.
No, I have never had kidney stones or any other kidney problems.
I had a bladder scope under anesthesia six months ago where they stretched my bladder and found small bleeding patches called Hunner lesions, but no catheters recently.
No, I do not have diabetes or any conditions that weaken my immune system.
I am sexually active with my husband and we use condoms, but intercourse has become very painful because of my bladder tenderness.
I drink moderate amounts of water, but I cannot hold my urine for long because the pelvic pain becomes agonizing.
Coffee, citrus fruits, spicy dishes, and carbonated beverages make the pain flare up significantly, as does emotional stress.
I am exhausted because I can never get a full night of sleep, and I can barely sit through meetings at work without running to the restroom.
I feel like the whole lining of my bladder is stripped raw like an open ulcer, which is why even a tiny bit of urine burns so terribly.
I'm scared I'm going to lose my job and ruin my marriage because I can't leave the bathroom for more than twenty minutes at a time.
I'm hoping to get some targeted medication to coat my bladder wall and finally give me enough pain relief to sit through a meeting.
I have high blood pressure and mildly elevated cholesterol, both diagnosed two years ago.
Aside from the cystoscopy with hydrodistension six months ago, I have never had any surgery or stayed in a hospital.
I take Lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day for my blood pressure; I do not take any over-the-counter medicines or supplements regularly.
I have no allergies to any medications or foods.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I do not drink alcohol at all, because even a single glass of wine makes my bladder pain unbearable.
I work as an office administrator and live with my husband; I try to stay active with light walks when the pain allows.
My mother has high blood pressure and my father has high cholesterol, but there is no family history of bladder or kidney diseases.
My menstrual cycles are regular every twenty-eight days, my last period started two weeks ago, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
Alert and in no acute distress, though looking fatigued and shifting uncomfortably from urinary urgency.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric without scars, distension, or visible masses.
Significant tenderness on deep palpation over the suprapubic area; abdomen is otherwise soft with no guarding or rebound tenderness.
Tympanic percussion note throughout the abdomen with no suprapubic dullness, and no distended urinary bladder is palpable.
No tenderness on percussion over bilateral costovertebral angles.

External genitalia appear normal without lesions; digital vaginal examination reveals marked tenderness along the anterior vaginal wall and hypertonic pelvic floor muscles, without cervical motion or adnexal tenderness.
